### `product-catalog`: you said `pod_unavailable`. They conclude `network_partition` (confidence: low).
Scope: Only product-catalog's serving path is affected: every GetProduct and ListProducts call to it from frontend, checkout and recommendation fails within about 1 ms, and it emits no spans or logs in the incident. Its own pod and container metrics keep arriving under the same pod name through the whole window, with uptime rising and no restart, so the instance is not shown to be gone. The callers' other traffic and the rest of the services were not shown to be affected beyond their calls to product-catalog, and the per-connection hubble metrics are absent in this case so the link itself could not be examined.
Ruled out:
- `pod_failure`: No restart: the pod name is the same (product-catalog-6456d7fcbb-26hwb) in normal and abnormal windows and k8s.pod.uptime rises without reset through about 02:05, so there is no kill-and-restart signature.

**Evidence against `pod_unavailable`**

- **The pod keeps emitting.** Across the abnormal window, the same pod (`product-catalog-6456d7fcbb-26hwb`) reports gauges (CPU, filesystem, memory, working set, page faults, node utilization) from 02:00:12 until 02:04:52. Its sum metrics (`container.cpu.time`, `k8s.pod.network.io`, `k8s.pod.network.errors`, `k8s.pod.uptime`) run to about 02:05:02. The normal window has the same metric set. Gauge sample counts in the incident are not lower than normal (71 vs 36 over the same ~5-minute span). The rubric's `pod_unavailable` signature is that metrics fall away; here they do not.

The `pod_unavailable` signature is partly met (silent spans and logs, fast-fail callers), but the metric-continuity part is not.
- The hubble per-connection metrics are missing in this case, so I could not check the link directly. Missing data means the link-level question is open, not answered.
